summary: Async normalization in SDK 1.4.0 causing cross-batch embedding mixing leading to duplicate top-k and tail latency for rerank
description:
Issue summary:
AtlasDocs (enterprise) reports intermittent duplicate results in rerank top-k and elevated tail latency after upgrading to Redwood SDK 1.4.0. Problem appears when customers stream embedding batches and call the /rerank endpoint concurrently.

Impact:
- Customer-visible: Users see duplicated candidates in top-5 and occasionally top-1, degrading UX for search/rank features.
- Performance: Tail latencies for rerank spike (99th percentile from ~120ms to ~2.3s) during affected windows.
- Scope: Reported on production in us-west region for AtlasDocs; similar but less frequent behavior observed in internal smoke tests.

Environment:
- Customer: AtlasDocs production (enterprise tenant) in us-west; heavy concurrent embedding ingestion plus rerank traffic.
- Redwood platform: hosted API (prod-us-west).
- SDK version: 1.4.0 (notable change: async L2-normalize flag enabled by default, batching/streaming rework).
- Models: redwood-embedder-v2 for on-the-fly embeddings; open-retriever-1.0 for reranker scoring.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Use SDK 1.4.0 with async_normalize=true and stream embeddings for ~200 concurrent requests (payloads of 5–20 documents each).
2) Immediately call /rerank for batched queries that overlap in time with embedding streams.
3) Observe rerank responses and latency distribution; duplicate IDs appear in top-k and 99p latency increases.

Observed logs / metrics / examples:
- APIGW trace ids: apigw-20260313-0812-az1 (customer trace), apigw-20260313-0829-az1 (internal repro).
- Sample rerank response (sanitized): top_k: [doc_124, doc_124, doc_7, doc_9, doc_3] — duplicate doc_124 appears twice with nearly identical scores.
- Serving runtime logs: buffered-queue: flush_count spikes aligned with duplicates; kv-cache hit-rate normal.
- SDK telemetry (from AtlasDocs): async_normalize.latency_hist: median 20ms, 99p 1.9s during incidents.

Initial hypothesis:
- Async L2-normalize introduced in SDK 1.4.0 performs normalization in a worker pool and re-emits normalized vectors back to the ingest path. Under high concurrency, a race may cause the same embedding ID to be enqueued twice (or the normalization callback to re-insert a completed vector), leading to duplicated vector presence in the local batch sent to rerank.
- Cross-batch memory of normalized vectors (cache-tagging bug) could cause mixes between adjacent streaming batches, producing near-duplicate vectors that bump tail latency due to reranker de-dup checks.

Attachments:
- reproducible_script.sh (internal repro harness), truncated logs attached in ticket thread.

Desired outcome:
- Identify root cause and provide a patch/workaround to prevent duplicate embeddings from being sent to rerank and to remove the tail-latency regression.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-13 08:20 PST: Customer reports first occurrence via support email.
- 2026-03-13 09:05 PST: Support triage; asked for traces and SDK version.
- 2026-03-13 10:10 PST: Engineering reproduced locally with SDK 1.4.0 and async_normalize=true; duplication repro consistent when worker_pool_size >= 8.
- 2026-03-13 14:30 PST: Heap/trace analysis shows duplicate enqueue events for same embed_id within ~12–18ms window.
- Hypothesis validated: race in SDK normalization callback can requeue the same payload on rare timing; also discovered missing idempotency check in local batch aggregator prior to dispatch to rerank.
- Quick check: toggling async_normalize=false returns system to baseline (no duplicates, tail latency normal).
resolution_notes:
Workaround (customer-facing):
- Instructed AtlasDocs to downgrade to SDK 1.3.x or set async_normalize=false in SDK 1.4.0 configuration. This reduced duplicates and restored tail latency to prior levels.

Engineering fixes in progress:
- SDK PR #4123 introduced to add an idempotency guard in the normalization callback and to ensure normalized vectors are deduplicated in the local batch aggregator. (PR link in related_github_prs).
- Serving-runtime alert rule adjusted to detect repeating embed_ids within a 50ms window and drop duplicates temporarily while fix is rolled out.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge SDK fix and ship 1.4.1 (patch) to customers; notify enterprise customers.
2) Enable additional telemetry around embed_id lifecycle in the platform for 72-hour monitoring post-rollout.
3) Confluence postmortem + recommended SDK flags added to upgrade guidance.
